subject: model parameters as outcome in other analyses

messages.author: 356316b848e93292
messages.subject: model parameters as outcome in other analyses
parts:
Hi all, 

I have conducted a multigroup CFA that fitted well and demonstrated scalar invariance. In the configural model, some model parameters (e.g., factor loadings, item thresholds) exhibited interesting group differences that I would like to closely examine. 

For instance, I am interested in knowing why the loading (or item threshold) for an item is higher in one group versus another, by treating the item loading as an outcome variable and regressing it on a number of other variables that I think might explain the group differences. 

Is this a reasonable analysis in SEM and doable in lavaan? If not, are there other analyses that may help me answer these sorts of questions? 

Appreciate it!
Frank

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: model parameters as outcome in other analyses
parts: Is this a reasonable analysis in SEM and doable in lavaan?
No, lavaan does not do mixtures.  Parameters are constants, not variables.
If not, are there other analyses that may help me answer these sorts of questions?

You can do MNLFA in OpenMx:

Kolbe, L., Molenaar, D., Jak, S., & Jorgensen, T. D. (2022). Assessing measurement invariance with moderated nonlinear factor analysis using the R package OpenMx. Psychological Methods. Advance online publication. https://doi.org/10.1037/met0000501

We posted the accepted version on the OSF with our online supplementary materials:  https://osf.io/6cyxt/

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
